concerns.text: The filtering criterion uses a minimum of 20 observations per species (Task T010), but the power analysis (Task T023) assumes a required minimum of 30 observations per species (SC‑009). This inconsistency can lead to under‑powered models when the filtered dataset contains species with 20‑29 samples.

Power analysis is performed on the post‑filtering dataset without accounting for the species‑stratified 5‑fold cross‑validation, which reduces the effective sample size per training fold. The reported power may therefore be overly optimistic.

Sensitivity analysis compares LMM coefficients to literature‑reported physiological ranges of nutrient concentrations, not to expected effect‑size ranges. This mismatch may conflate construct validity of the predictor (nutrient levels) with that of the effect (coefficients).

Missing‑nutrient handling first imputes species‑level means then applies k‑NN imputation. The bias assessment (Task T025) only evaluates leave‑one‑species‑out coefficient changes, which may not capture bias introduced by the two‑stage imputation.

Optional covariates (soil_moisture, temperature, elevation) are included only when available, but there is no systematic plan to assess their confounding impact or to ensure they are measured consistently across species.

VIF is computed only for phosphorus and nitrogen. If optional covariates are added, multicollinearity involving those variables is not checked, potentially violating the assumption of independent predictors.
